focus: Feed mechanism design: phrase specificity, author-signal scoring, render label, and four admission mechanisms compared
noveltyJustification: Scoring and render semantics were new evidence and the mechanism verdicts are new design decisions; several code paths were already known from iterations 1 and 4.
keyQuestions: Should _routes.yaml trigger phrases feed the advisor, and through which mechanism would that work?
answeredQuestions: Should _routes.yaml trigger phrases feed the advisor, and through which mechanism would that work?
ruledOut: Mechanism A: harvester extension to parse _routes.yaml
Mechanism B as primary: hand-written PHRASE_BOOSTS entries
One bridge per doctor command instead of per route

keyFindings.title: Phrase specificity scores 0.7 + 0.18 per extra token, capped at 1.0
Bridge signals enter through the explicit-author lane, not a new path
Command-kind candidates carry a 0.08 demotion without a slash in the prompt
The rendered brief label comes from the recommendation name, so bridges should render runnable command strings
Harvester extension rejected: new root and file type in two implementations
Hand PHRASE_BOOSTS rejected as primary: bypasses inventory, parity and drift guard
Allow-list admission supports per-route ids for multi-target commands
Recommended long-term: generate admission inputs from _routes.yaml and guard with CI
Input gate requires target-level bridge granularity and fully qualified names
The design problem is phrase arbitration, not vocabulary authoring

graphEvents.label: Per-route allow-list ids solve the collision
